question: After fixing the DistributedManager RSA key sharing bug by switching to HS256 symmetric JWT with shared TESTBED_SECRET, AND fixing numpy.bool_ JSON serialization, does C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 achieve CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure with n_non304>=800?
hypothesis: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 will be CONFIRMED on distributed multi-node infrastructure after fixing two bugs: (1) RSA key sharing: switch testbed_server.py from RS256 (per-process RSA keypair) to HS256 (shared TESTBED_SECRET env var), eliminating token cross-node invalidation; (2) JSON serialization: cast numpy.bool_ to bool() and handle NaN via None before json.dump at line 696. The parent MEASUREMENT_INVALID was caused entirely by these two infrastructure bugs (all distributed samples returned 401 due to RSA mismatch, and result.json failed to serialize). The grandparent's primary orthogonality metric independently confirms orthogonality on distributed infrastructure (stratified r=-0.0585, CI upper 0.0163<0.15, TOST p=2.03e-08, n_non304=688, audit PASS). LOCAL orthogonality is CONFIRMED across multiple experiments (r=0.023-0.047, n=684-844). With the RSA fix restoring valid-token 200 responses on distributed nodes and the JSON fix enabling proper metrics persistence, all C1-C7 conditions are expected to pass at n_non304>=800.
falsifier: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 on distributed infrastructure is REJECTED at delta=0.15 if ANY of the following occurs after the two fixes: (C1) behavioral detection mean TP < 0.85 OR mean TN < 0.85 on distributed infrastructure (after 304 exclusion); (C2) fewer than 2/3 endpoints have non-304 behavioral signal std > 0 OR fewer than 2/3 have non-304 structural signal std > 0; (C3) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 only) >= 0.15 on distributed testbed; (C4) TOST equivalence test p_upper >= 0.05 at delta=0.15 (one-sided, non-304 only); (C5) endpoint-stratified cache-mode heterogeneity: |r_stratified_enabled - r_stratified_disabled| >= 2 * SE_pooled; (C6) B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline shows |r| >= 0.15 (regression from LOCAL parent); (C7) B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED shows endpoint-stratified weighted |r| < 0.15 (confound fails to reproduce). C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents data collection or if n_non304 < 400.

baselines.description: Single-node Flask testbed WITHOUT concurrent load or multi-node distribution — identical to parent EXP-GRAPH-35572179326 and grandparent EXP-GRAPH-35538864957 LOCAL testbed. Regression-free baseline confirmation.
baselines.expected: |r| < 0.15, consistent with parent r=0.0233 and grandparent r=0.041

baselines.description: Multi-node distributed testbed: 2 independent Flask processes on separate ports (18971, 18972), each with independent SQLite database and in-memory CDN cache. Round-robin request routing. HS256 JWT with shared TESTBED_SECRET (fixing parent RSA bug). Each node independently generates ETag/Cache-Control headers. Cache invalidation on one node does NOT propagate to the other.

Single-node Flask testbed with 5 concurrent client sessions making simultaneous requests. Tests whether request contention, timing jitter, and interleaved cache states introduce behavioral-structural coupling.

Distributed negative control: same multi-node architecture as B-DISTRIBUTED but with V2 confound (fixed 'expired' request_id for expired responses, uuid4 for valid). Expected to reproduce the confound (|r| >= 0.15) across distributed nodes.
baselines.expected: |r| >= 0.15 (negative control confirming confound is genuine in distributed setting)

positive_control: Token validation failure detection on distributed infrastructure with HS256 shared secret: behavioral signal must correctly identify expired vs valid tokens with TP >= 0.85 across all distributed nodes. With shared TESTBED_SECRET, tokens created on node A are valid on node B, so valid-token requests return 200 (behavioral_delta ~0.0) and expired-token requests return 401 (behavioral_delta ~7.0). After 304 exclusion, all valid conditions should yield TN=1.0.
null_control: Structural signal std > 0 across all non-304 conditions on distributed infrastructure: independent ETag generation per node, Cache-Control headers, and UUID-based dynamic content should produce non-zero structural variation even on cache-disabled responses. Behavioral std should be non-zero on conditions with auth state variation.
measurement_validity: HS256 SYMMETRIC JWT FIX (PRIMARY): Switch testbed_server.py from RS256 (per-process RSA keypair via generate_rsa_keys()) to HS256 (shared TESTBED_SECRET env var). This eliminates the RSA key sharing bug where each Flask node generated independent RSA key pairs, causing round-robin routing to produce 100% 401 responses on valid tokens. The TESTBED_SECRET is already generated and passed to child processes by DistributedManager (run_experiment_distributed.py line 109: env['TESTBED_SECRET']=secrets.token_hex(32)). The fix modifies testbed_server.py to use jwt.encode/decode with HS256 algorithm and TESTBED_SECRET, removing the generate_rsa_keys() call and RSA public/private key variables.

JSON SERIALIZATION FIX: run_experiment_distributed.py at line 696 does json.dump(result) which fails on numpy.bool_ and NaN values. Fix: cast all metrics with float() and bool() native types before serialization, and handle NaN via None/null. This ensures result.json persists raw metrics instead of falling back to empty metrics/controls.

C1 304-EXCLUSION (inherited from grandparent): C1 behavioral detection control excludes 304 responses from TP/TN calculation. 304 cache-hit responses are HTTP caching artifacts, not behavioral signal changes.
V_ETAG_PERMISSION_LEAKAGE FIX (inherited from grandparent): testbed_server.py decodes expired JWT tokens WITHOUT verification to extract permission_level for ETag generation.
V3 ENDPOINT-STRATIFICATION (inherited from grandparent): Pooled Pearson r uses endpoint-stratified weighting, not simple concatenation.
V1 UUID FOR ALL STATUS CODES (inherited from grandparent): All request_ids use uuid.uuid4() for all status codes in primary testbed.
304 EXCLUSION: 304 responses excluded from pooled correlation, per-endpoint correlations, per-cache correlations, AND C1 behavioral detection control.
DISTRIBUTED INDEPENDENCE: Each Flask node has independent SQLite database, independent in-memory cache, independent ETag generation. No shared state between nodes except TESTBED_SECRET.
CACHE INDEPENDENCE: Cache invalidation on node A does NOT propagate to node B. Each node CDN simulation operates independently.
ROUND-ROBIN ROUTING: Distributed testbed routes requests round-robin across nodes. Each node receives approximately equal load.
NON-304 POWER: n >= 800 non-304 samples (target: 42 per condition per endpoint x 8 conditions x 3 endpoints = 1012 total, ~850 non-304 at 84% rate).
TOST ONE-SIDED: C3 tests CI upper < 0.15 only; C4 tests TOST p_upper < 0.05 only (one-sided).

Structural signal extraction uses ONLY: (a) ETag change (0/1), (b) Cache-Control change (0/1), (c) normalized Shannon entropy of UUID-based request_id, (d) SHA256(request_id)[:16] as int % 10000 / 10000.
Each endpoint has independent behavioral and structural signal extraction — no shared variables between signal domains.
decision_rule: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 on distributed infrastructure is CONFIRMED if ALL of: (C1) behavioral detection mean TP >= 0.85 AND mean TN >= 0.85 across all endpoints on distributed testbed (AFTER 304 EXCLUSION); (C2) at least 2/3 endpoints have non-304 behavioral signal std > 0 AND at least 2/3 have non-304 structural signal std > 0; (C3) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 samples only) < 0.15 on distributed testbed; (C4) TOST equivalence test p_upper < 0.05 at delta=0.15 (one-sided, non-304 samples only); (C5) endpoint-stratified cache-mode heterogeneity check (non-304 samples): |r_stratified_enabled - r_stratified_disabled| < 2 * SE_pooled; (C6) B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline shows |r| < 0.15 (no regression from parent); (C7) B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED shows endpoint-stratified weighted |r| >= 0.15 (negative control passes). C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is REJECTED if ANY condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents data collection or n_non304 < 400.
product_consequence_positive: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality confirmed on distributed production-like infrastructure with n_non304>=800. Parallel-channel architecture (separate behavioral and structural signal processing) is justified for multi-node deployment. Product may proceed with dual-signal freshness detection across distributed cache topologies. The RSA key sharing bug and JSON serialization bug are confirmed resolved.
product_consequence_negative: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality fails on distributed infrastructure even with HS256 shared secret and JSON fix. Parallel-channel architecture is NOT justified for multi-node deployment. Product must investigate cache-coupling as a correlation source and potentially use fused classifiers. Identifies a genuine distributed infrastructure barrier beyond the measurement artifacts.
estimated_cost: Low: (1) Fix HS256 symmetric JWT — modify testbed_server.py to use jwt.encode/decode with HS256 and TESTBED_SECRET instead of RSA keypair (~10 line change); (2) Fix JSON serialization — cast numpy types and handle NaN before json.dump (~5 line change); (3) Execute 4 conditions (B-LOCAL-ONLY, B-DISTRIBUTED, B-CONCURRENT, B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED) ~3-4 hours with 42 samples/condition/endpoint; (4) Analysis ~30 min. Total: 4-5 compute-hours. Infrastructure reused from parent.
expected_information_gain: Very high: this is the minimum cost experiment that resolves the primary unknown from parent EXP-GRAPH-35572179326 — whether C-FRESHNESS orthogonality achieves CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure. The two fixes are targeted code changes that directly address the sole reasons for the parent's MEASUREMENT_INVALID outcome. The grandparent's primary orthogonality metric already passes independently. A positive result (CONFIRMED) changes a product decision: parallel-channel architecture justified for multi-node deployment. A negative result (any C1-C7 fails after fixes) identifies a genuine distributed infrastructure barrier. Either outcome is high-information for C-FRESHNESS claim advancement.
